fact_text: The Pakistani banking sector earned about PKR 1,000 billion of profit before tax in 2024.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'National Bank of Pakistan - The return of the Dividend King' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst expects banking-sector profit before tax in 2025 to exceed the 2024 level of about PKR 1,000 billion.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'National Bank of Pakistan - The return of the Dividend King' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: When policy rates fall, a bank's yield on lending falls too, so the mix and cost of its deposits becomes the main earnings lever.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'National Bank of Pakistan - The return of the Dividend King' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Banks lend at broadly similar rates to government and private borrowers, because loan rates are linked to KIBOR, so funding cost differences come from deposits.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'National Bank of Pakistan - The return of the Dividend King' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Current account deposits are the cheapest funding for a bank because the depositor earns little or no return on them.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'National Bank of Pakistan - The return of the Dividend King' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Remunerative current accounts pay depositors a return further below the policy rate than ordinary savings accounts do, and the bank's spread on them is somewhat higher.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'National Bank of Pakistan - The return of the Dividend King' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: As interest rates fall, depositors move from savings into current accounts because the return gap looks small, which raises the current-account share of deposits.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'National Bank of Pakistan - The return of the Dividend King' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Falling rates raise the earnings of banks that hold large, sticky deposits, since their funding cost falls faster than the yield on their assets.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'National Bank of Pakistan - The return of the Dividend King' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: National Bank of Pakistan had the largest deposit base in the sector at the end of 2024.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'National Bank of Pakistan - The return of the Dividend King' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A 2024 court ruling ordered NBP to pay about PKR 60 billion in pension arrears to roughly 11,500 employees over the following years.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'National Bank of Pakistan - The return of the Dividend King' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The pension liability was already provisioned, so the 2024 ruling removed an uncertainty that had hung over the stock and became a positive trigger.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'National Bank of Pakistan - The return of the Dividend King' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: NBP's 2024 earnings were only about PKR 12 per share, because the pension expenses were booked in that single year.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'National Bank of Pakistan - The return of the Dividend King' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: NBP announced a PKR 8 per share dividend at the end of 2024, its first dividend in many years.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'National Bank of Pakistan - The return of the Dividend King' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's turnaround thesis for NBP rests on the combination of strong deposit growth, the end of the pension uncertainty, the removal of the minimum deposit rate, and dividend resumption.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'National Bank of Pakistan - The return of the Dividend King' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst expects NBP's 2025 deposit growth to be among the highest in the banking industry.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'National Bank of Pakistan - The return of the Dividend King' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: NBP's fixed-rate government securities bought at high yields keep earning well as policy rates fall, which supports its net interest income.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'National Bank of Pakistan - The return of the Dividend King' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The State Bank abolished the minimum deposit rate (MDR) requirement for non-individual savings accounts at the end of 2024, which had forced banks to pay savers a floor return.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'National Bank of Pakistan - The return of the Dividend King' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The MDR abolition helps NBP most because government and corporate savings form a large part of its deposits, so it can pay less on them.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'National Bank of Pakistan - The return of the Dividend King' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Each one percentage point of return saved on a PKR 1.5 trillion current-account base is worth roughly PKR 15 billion of income a year.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'National Bank of Pakistan - The return of the Dividend King' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Net interest income across the sector kept rising despite falling rates, because deposit growth, a higher current-account share and high-yield securities worked together.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'National Bank of Pakistan - The return of the Dividend King' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Bank share prices can rise when rates fall, because deposit growth, a rising current-account share and sticky fixed-rate income lift earnings, and lower rates tend to lift the P/E multiple the market pays.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'National Bank of Pakistan - The return of the Dividend King' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: NBP's president and CEO have worked at the bank for a long time, which the analyst sees as helpful for understanding the franchise and steering a turnaround.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'National Bank of Pakistan - The return of the Dividend King' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Management is revamping NBP's branches and making the bank more customer-centric, aiming to lift deposit growth and the current-account share.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'National Bank of Pakistan - The return of the Dividend King' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: NBP raised its dividend over the prior year in 2008, even during the global financial crisis, which the analyst cites as evidence of its dividend-stock history.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'National Bank of Pakistan - The return of the Dividend King' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: NBP had already earned about PKR 20 per share in the first half of 2025, based on the half-year results.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'National Bank of Pakistan - The return of the Dividend King' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's full-year 2025 earnings estimate for NBP is roughly PKR 38-40 per share, assuming the half-year trend continues.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'National Bank of Pakistan - The return of the Dividend King' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Management has indicated its dividend will be announced roughly in line with the prior year's payout ratio, which the analyst treats as a guide.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'National Bank of Pakistan - The return of the Dividend King' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst assumes a 60-65% payout ratio for 2025, which is somewhat below NBP's historical average, implying a dividend of roughly PKR 24-26 per share.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'National Bank of Pakistan - The return of the Dividend King' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's 2026 scenario assumes an average policy rate of 10%, deposits of about PKR 5 trillion and a current-account share near 30%.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'National Bank of Pakistan - The return of the Dividend King' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's 2026 scenario gives NBP net interest income of about PKR 260 billion.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'National Bank of Pakistan - The return of the Dividend King' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's 2026 scenario assumes operating expenses of about PKR 125 billion and provisioning of about 0.5% of the book, roughly PKR 10 billion.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'National Bank of Pakistan - The return of the Dividend King' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's 2026 scenario gives profit before tax of about PKR 175 billion and profit after tax of about PKR 85-90 billion, as the sector tax rate is assumed to fall each year.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'National Bank of Pakistan - The return of the Dividend King' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Converting the 2026 scenario profit into earnings per share gives roughly PKR 40-44 per share.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'National Bank of Pakistan - The return of the Dividend King' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The capital adequacy ratio, meaning the surplus equity a bank holds above requirements, is used as a proxy for its dividend-paying capacity.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'National Bank of Pakistan - The return of the Dividend King' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The State Bank requires banks to provision gradually against available-for-sale government securities, spread over a period of about three years.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'National Bank of Pakistan - The return of the Dividend King' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: NBP has already booked a large part of the required securities provisioning, so the remaining hit to its capital and dividend capacity is limited.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'National Bank of Pakistan - The return of the Dividend King' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Floods used to occur roughly once every 10 to 15 years in Pakistan, and the analyst notes they now arrive more often.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'National Bank of Pakistan - The return of the Dividend King' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Floods hit banks mainly through their agricultural lending, and the 2022 floods did not cause large losses across the sector.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'National Bank of Pakistan - The return of the Dividend King' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Much agricultural lending runs through government schemes that carry guarantees, which cushion banks against flood losses.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'National Bank of Pakistan - The return of the Dividend King' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: NBP is a major agricultural lender, and management has said its balance sheet should stay protected from floods as it was in 2022.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'National Bank of Pakistan - The return of the Dividend King' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: NBP has closed its New York branches and settled the penalties, and the analyst sees further surprises from the New York matter as unlikely.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'National Bank of Pakistan - The return of the Dividend King' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst values banks with dividend-yield and P/E approaches, and expects bull-market P/E improvement to lift bank multiples as well.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'National Bank of Pakistan - The return of the Dividend King' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: When Pakistan's economic indicators move in the right direction and the bull-market framework is on, PSX returns have historically been strong over one year.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'National Bank of Pakistan - The return of the Dividend King' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: When the rupee is stable, bull-market phases avoid a currency-driven discount on valuation multiples.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'National Bank of Pakistan - The return of the Dividend King' (YouTube transcript, undated)
